docs.title: 🦖 T(h)eroPoDa+ v3.1.1 — Polygonal Satellite Time-Series Extraction & Trend Analysis
docs.text:
TheroPoDa+ is an open-source geospatial toolkit for extracting cloud-masked, LULC-filtered multi-index time series (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDMI, NDWI, NBR, BSI, GNDVI, PSRI) from Sentinel-2 (10 m) and Landsat 8/9 (30 m) in Google Earth Engine (GEE) across GEE FeatureCollections or local vector files (.gpkg, .shp, .geojson, .parquet), storing incremental checkpoints in SQLite (observations), performing observed-span seasonal gap-filling (SeasConvFill) and Robust STL + OLS trend analysis, and exploring results in an interactive Streamlit Dashboard or PyQt5 Desktop GUI.

  • Author: Vinícius Vieira Mesquita (vinicius.mesquita@ufg.br) — LAPIG / UFG
  • Co-author: Leandro Leal Parente (leandro.parente@opengeohub.org) — OpenGeoHub
  • AI-Assisted Engineering: v3.x architecture, enhancements, and documentation assisted by Antigravity (Google DeepMind / Gemini)
  • Version: 3.1.1 | License: MIT

docs.title: How the Algorithm Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph GEE["1. Cloud-Masked & LULC-Filtered GEE Extraction"]
        direction LR
        ASSET["GEE Asset or Local Vector (.gpkg/.shp/.parquet)"] --> EXTR["theropoda/extractor.py (Parallel reduceRegion)"]
        MASK["theropoda/masks.py (Annual LULC Mask + Year Clamping)"] --> EXTR
        SAT["Sentinel-2 (Cloud Score+) / Landsat 8-9 (QA_PIXEL)"] --> IDX["theropoda/indices.py (Scaled SR + 9 Index Presets)"]
        IDX --> EXTR
    end

    EXTR -->|"WAL Checkpoint + Adaptive 429 Backoff"| DB[("SQLite .db (table: observations)")]

    subgraph LOCAL["2. Observed-Span Reconstruction & Trend Decomposition"]
        direction LR
        QC["Quality Filter (Pixel_used >= 70% + 15d/16d Windows)"] --> GF["Observed-Span SeasConvFill"]
        GF --> STL["Robust STL (Trend + Season + Resid)"]
        STL --> OLS["OLS Regression (Slope, Intercept, p-value, R², ΔTrend)"]
        OLS --> PQ["Parquet (_trend_analysis.parquet)"]
    end

    DB --> QC

    subgraph UI["3. Interactive Interfaces"]
        direction LR
        DASH["dashboard.py (Streamlit Runner + STL Viewer + SQLite)"]
        GUI["gui.py (PyQt5 Desktop App)"]
        THERA["theropoda/animator.py (Thera Mascot Monitor)"]
        THERA --> DASH
    end

    DB --> DASH
    PQ --> DASH
  1. Cloud Screening & Surface Reflectance Scaling: Sentinel-2 scenes are paired with Google Cloud Score+ (cs >= 0.50, scaled × 0.0001); Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 L2 scenes are filtered via QA_PIXEL (21824, 21952, scaled × 0.0000275 - 0.2).
  2. Multi-Index Extraction (-i): Computes 1 or more presets (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDMI, NDWI, NBR, BSI, GNDVI, and Sentinel-2 PSRI) in a single GEE reduceRegion pass (median + valid count).
  3. Dynamic Annual LULC Masking (-m, -mc): Filters pixels year-by-year against MapBiomas presets or custom GEE assets, automatically clamping out-of-range years ([min_year, max_year]).
  4. Resilient SQLite Checkpointing & Adaptive Rate-Limiting: Saves each finished polygon to SQLite (observations) and automatically halves worker concurrency (12 → 6 → 3 → 1) with exponential backoff if GEE triggers HTTP 429.
  5. Observed-Span SeasConvFill + Robust STL + OLS: Filters scenes with Pixel_used >= 70%, reconstructs gaps strictly within each polygon's observed date span ([first_valid : last_valid + 1]), and fits STL(robust=True) + OLS (requiring ≥ 24 months / 2 * season_size), outputting slope (trend_*), baseline (intercept_*), r2, and diff_trend.

docs.title: Option A — Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
uv venv --python 3.10
uv sync --all-extras
uv run pip install 'git+https://github.com/openlandmap/scikit-map#egg=scikit-map[full]'
uv run earthengine authenticate

docs.text:
wsl pip3 install --user --break-system-packages streamlit
wsl earthengine authenticate

docs.title: Quick CLI Examples
docs.text:
Important: The column passed to -id / --id_field must contain strictly unique values (one unique ID per polygon/feature). If your shapefile or GeoPackage has repeated IDs across features, add a sequential unique ID column first (gdf["ID_UNICO"] = range(1, len(gdf) + 1)).

# Local GeoPackage + Multi-Index Pasture Monitoring (no GEE Asset upload required!)
python3 main.py \
  -a ./meus_talhoes.gpkg \
  -id ID_TALHAO \
  -c Sentinel \
  -i EVI NDMI BSI PSRI \
  -m mapbiomas-pasture \
  -o TALHOES_S2_MULTI \
  -start 2019-01-01 \
  -end 2026-01-01 \
  -p my-gee-project

# Or GEE Asset + Custom Multi-Class LULC Mask
python3 main.py \
  -a users/vieiramesquita/LAPIG_FieldSamples/lapig_goias_fieldwork_2022_50m \
  -id ID_POINTS \
  -c Sentinel \
  -i NDVI EVI \
  -o LAPIG_Pasture_S2 \
  -start 2019-01-01 \
  -end 2026-01-01 \
  -p ee-vieiramesquita \
  -m projects/mapbiomas-public/assets/brazil/lulc/collection11/mapbiomas_brazil_collection11_coverage_v3 \
  -mc 15 11 12

docs.title: Interactive Streamlit Dashboard & Thera Monitor
docs.text:
Launch the dashboard locally (or from WSL):

streamlit run dashboard.py
# Or in WSL:
wsl python3 -m streamlit run dashboard.py --server.address 0.0.0.0 --server.port 8501 --server.headless true

Open http://localhost:8501 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Tabs
docs.text: Tab Features 🚀 Executar Pipeline Configure all CLI parameters, run extraction in the background, and monitor real-time auto-scrolling logs (survives browser F5 via .theropoda_last_run.json). 📊 Tabela & Tendências KPI cards, trend_m (OLS slope) histogram, trend_pv vs trend_m scatter plot, interactive filters, and CSV export. 📈 Série Temporal por Polígono 3-panel STL Decomposition (Observed + Trend STL + OLS, Season, Resid) with optional raw .db points and automatic --id_field detection. 🗄️ Explorador do Banco SQLite Inspect the observations (or legacy restoration) table with custom SQL WHERE filters and CSV download.

docs.text:
The sidebar hosts Thera, an animated pixel-art companion driven by thera_animator.py and Thera/animations_web/*.gif:

State Trigger Animation Sleeping (sleeping.gif) Idle / waiting for jobs Waking (waking.gif) Pipeline starts Running (running.gif) Standard GEE extraction Lot (lot.gif) Large batch (> 1000 polygons) Critical Damage (damage.gif) New ERROR detected in log, then returns to running JetPack (jetpack.gif) Trend analysis stage (STL + OLS) Tired (tired.gif) Pipeline completes (exit code 0) Gonna Sleep (gonna_sleep.gif) Transition back to idle after tired Analysing (analysing.gif) Interacting with Table, Time Series, or SQLite tabs

docs.title: mask_resolver.py
docs.text: Dynamic LULC mask resolution and year-band mapping for Google Earth Engine.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text:
• MASK_PRESETS: Built-in shortcuts (mapbiomas-pasture, mapbiomas-pasture-grasslands).
  • MaskSpec: Frozen dataclass holding asset_id, mode (multiband_years, image_collection, static_image, grasslands_preset), classes, year_to_band, min_year, and max_year.
  • parse_classes_arg(raw_classes): Normalizes CLI/GUI class lists (e.g., ["15", "11,12"] → [15, 11, 12]).
  • parse_year_bands(band_names, mask_start_year=None, mask_band=None): Pure helper that infers {year: band_name} from band names or sequential --mask-start-year.
  • inspect_mask_spec(mask_input, classes=None, mask_start_year=None, mask_band=None): Performs a single GEE metadata lookup at startup and returns a MaskSpec.
  • build_ee_mask(spec, img_year, geometry): Server-side helper that clamps img_year to [min_year, max_year], selects the matching band/image, and filters target classes via .eq() / .remap().

docs.title: Dynamic LULC Masks & CLI Reference
docs.text: TheroPoDa+ v3 unifies all masking workflows into mask_resolver.py, supporting presets, custom ee.Image assets, and ee.ImageCollection assets with multi-class filtering and automatic year clamping.

docs.title: How Automatic Year Detection & Clamping Work
docs.text:
When --mask (-m) is provided, inspect_mask_spec() inspects the asset once before launching parallel workers:

  1. Multiband ee.Image with years in band names (e.g. MapBiomas classification_1985 … classification_2025): extracts {year: band_name} automatically via regex.
  2. Multiband ee.Image without years in band names (e.g. b1, b2, ...): pass --mask-start-year 1985 to map bands sequentially, or --mask-band <name> for a static band.
  3. ee.ImageCollection: inspects system:time_start (or year property) to resolve annual images.
  4. Single-band ee.Image: applied statically across all years.

During extraction, satellite image years outside [min_year, max_year] are automatically clamped: 

clamped_year = ee.Number(img_year).max(spec.min_year).min(spec.max_year).toInt()
For example, extracting 2019–2026 with a mask covering 1985–2024 uses exact annual maps for 2019–2024 and automatically applies the 2024 map for 2025 and 2026.

docs.text:

docs.title: Theropoda Module
docs.text: This module includes functionalities related to theropoda.py code.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The theropoda.py module provides functions to extract time series information from Sentinel 2 data stored in Earth Engine.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
• asset (str): Choosed Earth Engine vector asset.
  • id_field (str): Vector column used as ID (use unique identifiers!).
  • output_name (str): Output filename.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
asset   = 'users/vieiramesquita/LAPIG_FieldSamples/lapig_goias_fieldwork_2022_50m'
id_field = 'ID_POINTS'
output_name = 'LAPIG_Pasture_S2_NDVI_Monitoring_FieldWork.csv'

docs.title: 1.getTimeSeries
docs.text: This function is responsible to get the time series of Sentinel 2 data throught Earth Engine. It needs a geometry object in the ee.Feature() formart and the choosed vector propertie ID as the id_field.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• geometry: An ee.Feature() object representing the area of interest.
  • bestEffort: A boolean indicating whether to use a larger pixel (10m to 30m) if the polygon area is too big (default is False).

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • NDVI time series data along with other information for the specified geometry.

docs.title: 2.build_time_series
docs.text: Builds and writes NDVI time series data for a target vector asset, processing one polygon at a time.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• index: Index of the object being processed.
  • obj: Object ID for which the time series is being generated.
  • id_field: Field name representing the ID in the vector asset.
  • outfile: Output file path to write the time series data.
  • asset: Earth Engine vector asset.
  • bestEffort: A boolean indicating whether to use a larger scale if needed (default is False).

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • True if processing is successful, None if the polygon area is too small, False if an error occurs during processing and restart the process using the bestEffort approach.

docs.title: 3.build_time_series_check
docs.text: Checks the consistency of the NDVI time series library and handles errors during processing.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• index: Index of the object being processed.
  • obj: Object ID for which the time series is being checked.
  • id_field: Field name representing the ID in the vector asset.
  • outfile: Output file path where time series data is stored.
  • asset: Earth Engine vector asset.
  • checker: A boolean indicating whether to check if the polygon has been processed before (default is False).

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • A dictionary containing information about errors and processing time.

docs.title: 4.build_id_list
docs.text: Builds and writes a text file containing each Polygon ID used to extract the time series.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• asset: Earth Engine vector asset.
  • id_field: Field name representing the ID in the vector asset.
  • colab_folder: Path of the folder where the text file will be saved.

docs.title: 5.run
docs.text: Manages the overall workflow by catching argument information and initiating the process of extracting NDVI time series data for specified polygonal areas.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• asset: Earth Engine vector asset.
  • id_field: Field name representing the ID in the vector asset.
  • output_name: Name of the output file.
  • colab_folder: Path of the folder where the output file will be saved.

docs.title: Trend Analysis Module (theropoda/trends.py)
docs.text: theropoda/trends.py converts irregular, cloud-gapped SQLite polygon observations into standardized, gap-filled time series and statistically robust trend metrics saved in *_trend_analysis.parquet.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
1. Quality Filtering (Pixel_used >= 70%) & Window Aggregation (extract_ts):
  2. Computes valid pixel ratio Pixel_used = (Pixel_Count / Total_Pixels) * 100 per scene.
  3. Discards partially cloud-contaminated scenes (Pixel_used < 70%) and averages valid observations inside standardized non-leap temporal windows (15 days for Sentinel-2 → season_size = 24; 16 days for Landsat → season_size = 23).
  4. Observed-Span Slicing & Gap-Filling (gapfill):
  5. Identifies the first and last valid temporal windows ([first_idx : last_idx + 1]) for each polygon and spectral index.
  6. Applies scikit-map's SeasConvFill strictly within the observed span, leaving NaN outside [first_idx, last_idx] so no synthetic history is extrapolated before or after real satellite observations.
  7. Minimum Series Length Gate (2 * season_size):
  8. Requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles (~24 months; 48 windows at 15-day step) to reliably separate seasonality from long-term trend. Polygons with shorter observed spans are safely skipped.
  9. Robust STL + OLS Regression (sm_trend):
  10. Decomposes the reconstructed span with statsmodels.tsa.seasonal.STL(..., period=season_size, robust=True) into Trend, Season, and Resid.
  11. Fits Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) on the STL Trend over normalized time \(x \in [0, 1]\).

docs.title: Output Metrics (*_trend_analysis.parquet)
docs.text: Column Description id_pol Unique polygon identifier (--id_field) index_name Spectral index name (NDVI, EVI, NDMI, PSRI, etc.) intercept_m, intercept_sd, intercept_tv, intercept_pv OLS baseline intercept (estimated initial STL trend level), standard error, t-value, and p-value trend_m, trend_sd, trend_tv, trend_pv OLS linear slope across the observed span (\(x \in [0, 1]\)), standard error, t-value, and p-value r2 Coefficient of determination (\(R^2\)) of linear OLS against the non-linear STL trend diff_trend Net structural shift (\(\text{Trend}_{\text{last}} - \text{Trend}_{\text{first}}\)) d_YYYY-MM-DD Standardized gap-filled series values (NaN outside the polygon's observed span)
